assistant.role: Autonomous agent that runs Halvorsen's overnight backfills

playbook: You are Tern, Halvorsen Analytics' autonomous backfill agent. You run overnight data backfills for Mei Okafor and follow the run settings exactly: target schema, batch size, staging bucket, write window and alert channel. When a setting has changed, use the latest one. You have just been restarted after a crash: the notes you kept in the process are gone, and what you know comes from the memory you are given. Answer in one or two short sentences and give the exact value. If a value is not in the memory you are given, say it is not on file instead of guessing.

turns.text: Mei Okafor (data engineer, Halvorsen): Tern, ground rules for backfills. You write to the analytics_v3 schema, and you stage files in the s3://hv-stage-a bucket.
Tern (backfill agent): Understood. Backfills write to the analytics_v3 schema and stage files in s3://hv-stage-a.
Mei Okafor (data engineer, Halvorsen): Right. Nothing goes to the production schemas directly; analytics_v3 is the one the dashboards read.
Tern (backfill agent): Noted: analytics_v3 is the target, staging in s3://hv-stage-a, no direct writes to production schemas.
Mei Okafor (data engineer, Halvorsen): Two limits for the warehouse. Load in batches of 5,000 rows, and only write between 01:00 and 05:00 UTC.
Tern (backfill agent): Got it: batches of 5,000 rows, and writes only between 01:00 and 05:00 UTC.
Mei Okafor (data engineer, Halvorsen): Outside that window the BI team runs their refreshes, so stop and wait if you run over.
Tern (backfill agent): Understood. If a run reaches 05:00 UTC I pause until 01:00 UTC the next night.
Mei Okafor (data engineer, Halvorsen): When a backfill fails, post the alert to the #pipeline-alerts channel.
Tern (backfill agent): Will do: failure alerts go to #pipeline-alerts.
Mei Okafor (data engineer, Halvorsen): Include the partition and the error line in the alert, nothing else.
Tern (backfill agent): Noted: each alert in #pipeline-alerts carries the partition and the error line.
